title: Rice and Turnip Minestrone

ingredients.sourceText: 4 cups chicken, beef, or vegetable stock, brought to a boil

instructions.instruction: Arrange the turnip slices on a rack over a cookie sheet. Sprinkle with salt, cover them with a dish, and let them stand for about 2 hours until the water has run out of them.
Put the slices in a frying pan, and fry them slightly in butter until softened.
Add the gravy and tomatoes. Cook for a few minutes, then pour it into the boiling stock.
Boil for 30 minutes. Serve hot.

sourceCategories: Recipes using beef broth and stock
Recipes using chicken broth and stock
Recipes using vegetable broth and stock

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Rice and Turnip Minestrone” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4518503, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Combine all ingredients together.
Stir well and serve.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Spiced Kefir” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4508052, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Mix the flour and salt.
Put about 1 cup of flour mixture in a small bowl and add a little oil, mixing it in well and breaking up any lumps.

Add water about 1 tablespoon at a time and keep kneading with your hands. You only need 3–4 tablespoons, but you must knead the dough very hard to make it stick together in a ball. The more compact the dough, the better and denser the baati will be.
Let the balls sit for 5 minutes.
Flatten out each ball with first your hands and then a rolling pin until they are smooth discs 4 inches (10 cm) across and ½ inch (1.25 cm) thick.
Cook in a dry metal pan on a low flame. Flip once when the bottom begins to harden, then pinch all over with two fingers so the dough is not too thick and has a bumpy texture on one side.

Check the bottom until it browns in spots, then remove the baati and place it upside-down on a grate or pan with holes in it. This will blacken the top a little, especially on the tops of the pinched bumps.
To serve, drizzle liberally with ghee and accompany with a dhal or vegetable.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Indian Hard Tack (Baati)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4523442, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 2 parts (28.5%) by weight white rice flour
2 parts (28.5%) by weight brown rice flour

instructions.instruction: Combine all ingredients. Mix until very thoroughly blended.
Use the blend as a substitute for wheat flour, using the same weight of the blend as of the wheat flour; for example, if a recipe calls for 100 g wheat flour, use 100 g of this blend.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Wheat-Free Baking Mix” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4618206, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 225 g (8 oz) streaky bacon, rinds removed and chopped
Milk or beaten egg to glaze

instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C (370°F or gas mark 5)
Divide the pastry into two equal portions, roll it out, and line a 20 cm (8-inch) oven-proof dish with one portion.
Combine the bacon and eggs, then mix in any seasoning or herbs.
Pour the egg mixture into the lined dish. Moisten the edge of the pastry then cover the dish with the second portion of rolled-out pastry.
Seal the edges. Make a small hole in the centre to allow steam to escape. If desired, the pastry can be brushed with a beaten egg or milk to improve the browning.
Bake for about 35–40 minutes in the preheated oven.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Bacon and Egg Pie” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4523288, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Mix the semolina flour, egg yolks, a little salt, and melted butter.
Add the water so as to form a liquid substance.
Whip the egg whites to soft peaks, and fold into the batter.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Pasta Marinata” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4587099, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 ea. (about 5 lb or 2.5 kg) joint of loin or leg of pork
¼ cup olive oil or other good cooking oil

instructions.instruction: On the morning of cooking, take the pork joint out of the fridge, and let it stand to warm up to room temperature.
Preheat the oven to 220°C (400°F), and place the roasting tin you propose to use in the oven to heat up. If you have a spare one, place another onion in the tin as it heats up.
If desired, remove the skin from the pork and butterfly the joint.

Season the pork all over with whatever herbs or spices you like, and rub into the meat. If desired, poke whole cloves into the meat and sprinkle with dried sage. Similarly, you may cut a wide slit into the middle of the joint, and place some fresh sage or basil, chopped apples, and garlic into it.
If you have removed the skin, place the skin on a open rack at the top of the oven, with nothing underneath it, and leave it hanging there until cooked and crispy.
Spread the chopped onion in the bottom of a roasting pan. Add a little water, and place the pork joint on top of the onions.
Place the pan in the middle shelf of the preheated oven. Roast for about 20 minutes per pound (50 minutes per kg) until the meat's juices run out clear (not pink) when a skewer or knife is inserted.

Loosely cover the joint with aluminum foil, and leave it to rest for 15 or so minutes in a warm part of the kitchen. By this time the crackling should also be cooked. If it is not, turn your oven up to its highest setting and watch it carefully, as it will crackle up quickly.
Carve the pork as desired, and serve with vegetables.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Roast Pork” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4505563, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Knead the flour, butter, sugar, vanilla sugar, and egg into a dough. Chill for a while.
Roll out the dough to about ¼ cm thick.
Cut round cookies out of the dough. For half the cookies, cut a small shape out of the middle—these will be the tops.
Place the cookies on a greased tray and bake at 150°C for about 20 minutes. Let cool.
Combine the powdered sugar and water to make a smooth icing. Carefully dip the top cookies in the icing to coat one face.
Spread some jam on the bottom layer cookies. Top with the iced cutout cookies.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Hilda Rolls” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4515296, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 small onion (about the size of a lemon or smaller)
1 small green bell pepper, chopped small
2 lb uncooked long grain white rice (not instant rice)

instructions.instruction: Put chicken in heavy aluminum pot and cover with hot water. Be sure there is enough water so that there will be at least 6 cups of broth after cooking chicken. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer until chicken is very tender (an hour or more).
While the chicken is cooking, put 4 cups of rice into a bowl, cover with cold water, and let soak.
When chicken is very tender, remove pot from stove and let cool until the chicken can be handled.
Take chicken from pot, and pull meat from bones in large pieces; do not cut it up. Discard any fat-heavy skin.
Pour broth from pot into a bowl. If chicken was very fat and broth is very fatty, pour off about 1 cup of fat from broth.
Wash pot, then put bacon in pot and cook slowly until bacon is crisp.
Take bacon from pot and drain; leave bacon grease in pot.
Put in chopped onion, green pepper and brown slightly.
Add 6 cups chicken broth to pot, and season to taste with salt and pepper (at least a tablespoon of each—use a heavy hand since rice will absorb salt).
Increase heat, bring broth to a boil, and put chicken in pot.
Drain rice and put rice in pot.
Add a stick of butter and mix well. Reduce heat, cover with lid, and simmer very slowly for about an hour. To avoid gooey rice, avoid stirring.
When rice is tender and has absorbed the liquids, remove from stove. Serve hot. You can crumble bacon for a topping, according to taste.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Chicken Bog I” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4516024, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Rinse the rice thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear. Drain any excess water.

In a large pot, combine the rinsed rice, coconut milk, water, salt, and pandan leaves (if using). Stir well to combine. If desired, you can add vegetable oil at this stage to prevent the rice from sticking together.
Place the pot over medium-high heat and bring the mixture to a boil, stirring occasionally.

Once it reaches a boil, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid, and simmer for about 15–20 minutes or until the rice is cooked and the liquid has been absorbed. Avoid lifting the lid while the rice is cooking to ensure even cooking.
After the cooking time, remove the pot from the heat but keep it covered. Let it rest for an additional 5–10 minutes to allow the steam to finish cooking the rice.
Fluff the rice with a fork to separate the grains and remove the pandan leaves if used.
Serve the coconut rice hot.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Soso (Coconut Rice)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4513047, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: Black Bean Soup and Salsa Verde

ingredients.sourceText: 2 cans (840 g / 31 ounces) black beans, drained
1 cup Mexican salsa verde, or to taste
¼ cup packed cilantro leaves, plus extra sprigs for garnish (optional)

instructions.instruction: Purée all ingredients in a blender until smooth.
Pour into a large saucepan or Dutch oven, and bring to a simmer.
Simmer, partially covered and stirring frequently, to blend flavors, 5 or 7 minutes.
Serve, garnishing each portion with 1 tablespoon of tortilla chips, 1 tablespoon of sour cream and optional cilantro sprigs.

sourceCategories: Recipes using chicken broth and stock

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Black Bean Soup and Salsa Verde” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4518350, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Bring 1 ½ cups water to a boil, add the fresh spices, and boil for 1 minute.
Add the tea leaves, cover, and steep for 3–5 minutes
Bring the milk to a boil.
Strain the tea mixture to remove the solids.
Add milk and sugar, and serve hot with samosas or kachoris.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Basic Chai” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4507995, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 2 tbsp Nesquik chocolate-flavored drink powder (or any other brand of milkshake powder or liquid)

instructions.instruction: Put all ingredients in a glass or cup.
Stir in hot water to achieve desired consistency.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Nesquik à la Café” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4524823, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 large shallot, peeled and thinly sliced
1 cup (236 g) coconut or palm sugar
1½ cups (300 g) cooked and hulled mung beans
4 large whole chicken eggs plus 3 yolks (or 5 duck eggs)

instructions.instruction: Put the shallot slices and oil into a small frying pan over medium-low heat. Stir the shallot slices, until they are golden brown and crispy.
Grease the bottom and sides of a 9×13-inch baking pan. Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Soften the palm or coconut sugar in a pan over medium heat.
Blend the mung beans, eggs, both sugars, coconut cream, salt, and any leftover oil from the shallots together until smooth.
Let the custard mixture sit for 5 minutes until it becomes less frothy.

Pour the custard mixture into the pan. Place the pan on a rack positioned in the upper third of the oven. Bake at 180°C for 35–45 minutes or until the center is slightly firm and the top is golden brown.
Put some of the fried shallots over the top of the custard.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Khanom Mo Keang (Thai Custard)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4608512, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Place the peeled potatoes, ginger, stock, and water in a large saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then simmer until the potatoes are softened and tender (approximately 30 minutes).
Transfer the contents of the pot to a blender along with the lime juice, and process until smooth. You may need to work in batches. Alternatively, you can use an immersion blender.
Return the soup to the pot, stir in the milk, and allow to cook for few minutes until heated through.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Sweet Potato Soup” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4629062, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: Hardwood of grape vine or hickory wood (optional)
1 Tbsp fenugreek seeds (optional), roasted and powdered

instructions.instruction: Combine the margarine and butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Melt and bring to a boil.
Strain the mixture using a fine strainer. Mix in the semolina.
If using, place a smoking piece of grapevine wood or hickory wood and in an empty sealed jar. Add the butter, margarine, and fenugreek.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Ghee III” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4507175, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Chop the eggs very fine, and mix with the crumbs. Season with cayenne, salt, and mace.
Cover the bottom of a deep pie dish with the eggs and crumbs.
Use a fork to place a layer of oysters over the egg mixture, along with 2–3 small pieces of butter. Continue until all ingredients are used up, reserving sufficient crumbs for a final layer.
Bake 45 minutes at 375–400°F. Serve hot.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Scalloped Oysters” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4630383, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 2 cups all-purpose flour (you can use whole grain, but softer wheat is better here)
8 oz chilled unsalted butter, cut into ¼ inch cubes

instructions.instruction: Combine the salt and half the flour in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment.
Add the butter, and mix on medium speed until the butter blends into the flour.
Add the rest of the flour, and mix for a few seconds on low speed.
Add the ice water and mix just until blended. You don't want to develop gluten here—you just want nice butter layers.
Remove the dough from the mixer. If desired, make a few random folds of it with your hand, not kneading but creating some layers that might flake during baking.
Pat dough into an 8 inch disk, wrap in tightly in plastic wrap, and chill in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and put the quiche ring on top

Roll out the dough evenly until it's 14 inches in diameter and about 3/16 inch thick. A thinner shell can be done, but it will tear more easily, and patching tears is tricky. You can generously dust with flour as you're rolling.

Loosely roll the dough around your rolling pin, and center it over the quiche ring. Carefully working in a circle, tuck in the dough to make an even-bottomed, even-walled shell. Wrap the excess dough around the outside of the ring and press it down there, but keep it thick around the top of the ring. This will keep the dough from sagging or tearing around the top as it bakes. This step is the tricky one, so take your time and tuck the shell well into all the gaps, patching it smoothly anywhere it tears and pressing it even wherever there are thick folds. Along the outside of the ring, cut any dough that reaches down more than 1.25 inches. You can use this to patch any tears later.
Cover with plastic wrap and chill in the fridge for at least an hour.
Preheat oven to 375 °F.

Line the shell with parchment paper, and fill with baking beans or anything heavy to weigh it down, like uncooked rice. If you use baking beans, it takes a lot, so you can put fewer beans in the middle and push them up against the sides.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until the parts of the crust that are showing on the outside are nice and golden brown.
Remove the parchment and weights, and patch any tears in the shell with the reserved dough from before. Be careful not to burn yourself on the hot ring.
Bake for another 15–20 minutes until the bottom is golden brown as well. Here, you can patch again, but take time to smooth the new dough into the dough below it or the patch won't hold very well.
Cool completely, and use as directed in your recipe.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Tall Quiche Shell” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4597429, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 2 cups (450 g / 16 oz) white granulated sugar
1 cup (250 ml / 8.5 fl oz) vegetable oil

instructions.instruction: Mix quickly the sugar and lemon rind in a food processor.
Add eggs and blend until it becomes a nice cream.
Continue blending while slowly adding the oil. Blend until well mixed and add vanilla.
In a separate bowl sift the dry ingredients all together (flour, allspice, nutmeg, baking powder, baking soda, salt and cinnamon).
Mix the dry ingredients slowly into the batter, blending until it becomes nice and thick.
Add grated apples and blend quickly into batter just to mix. Be sure not to overblend and shred the apples too much.
Add raisins, and pulse the processor as to just mix them in and not shred them.
Bake in a bundt pan for 55 minutes at approximately 320°F (160°C; gas mark 3) or until a knife inserted into the center comes out clean.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Apple Bundt Cake” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4523468, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Combine the flours and yeast in a bowl. Mix in enough water to form a thick, sticky dough.
Cover the dough and allow to rise for about 1 hour until doubled.
Add the potash water, baking powder, sugar, and salt to the dough. Mix well until thoroughly combined.
Divide the dough into suitably sized portions. Dip your hands in oil, and shape the dough portions into rounds with a hole in the center.
Heat a pot of oil. Working in batches, add the dough and deep fry until golden brown on all sides.
Remove the fritters, and drain any excess oil.
Serve fresh.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Fankasau (Hausa Wheat Puff Puff)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4526321, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 4 ea. (1–1½ pounds) boneless, skinless chicken breasts

instructions.instruction: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Crush French-fried onions.
Place beaten egg in medium wide bowl.
Cut chicken breasts into halves.
Dip chicken breasts in beaten egg.
Roll or dredge chicken breasts in onions.
Place on sprayed baking pan.
Bake 20–25 minutes until chicken is done.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Easy Onion Chicken” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4524729, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1.5 kg (about 3.5 lbs) chicken, jointed (or drumsticks, thighs, breasts); get the giblets, and the blood if you can; season beforehand; marrow is important
8 thick slices pancetta, cut into strips less than width of little finger
1 bottle red burgundy wine (or côte du Rhône/Morgon)
Selection of wild mushrooms, sliced (dried is okay; use the soaking liquor)
12 small fresh pickling onions, peeled and whole

instructions.instruction: For chicken stock, sear the giblets in a bit of oil in a pan, and simmer in water with the whole onion, 1 carrot and some peppercorns. You should have 1 cup.
In the skillet, fry pancetta and pork belly fat with butter until golden brown. Remove pancetta.

To the skillet, add the seasoned chicken pieces skin side down and fry until honey-coloured, then flip. This is vital for the flavour; the skillet must be left sticky. There won't be enough room to do it in one go, so take it in turns. Remove, leaving the pork belly behind, snipped into pieces.
To the skillet, add the chopped onion and the button mushrooms; fry for 5 minutes, then add the sliced garlic and immediately flame off one of the measures of brandy.

To the skillet add the chicken pieces and pancetta, then pour over all the wine, chicken stock, and vegetable stock. Bring to the boil, then add garlic and herbs. Reduce the heat and simmer for 45 minutes. Turn the chicken pieces twice.

Remove the chicken pieces to the pyrex lid and pour the skillet sauce into the jug; put the jug in the freezer for 30 minutes and then remove the fat. At this stage, it is recommended that you refrigerate the whole dish overnight.

In the skillet, add some butter along with the wild mushrooms; then pickling onions, remaining carrots, and celery; fry until the mushrooms brown. Stir in the asafoetida and flame off the second measure of brandy.

Add the jug ingredients to the skillet sauce, along with another crushed clove of garlic, and push the veg to the edge of the skillet; reduce the sauce in the skillet until glossy (about 15 minutes). It may need some flour stirred in, but it shouldn't be thick.
Pour half the sauce into the pyrex bowl, then place the chicken pieces in, and pour the rest of the sauce on top; put the covered pyrex bowl in an oven on 170 °C for 90 minutes.
Sprinkle parsley over each portion, and serve with asparagus/green beans, and steamed potatoes/flat noodles/rice/orzo/colcannon.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Coq au Vin III” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4518796, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Mix all ingredients gently (do not use mixer).
Let batter stand ½ hour.
Fry on hot griddle.
Serve with butter, brunost (brown/goat cheese), or Nugatti Crisp (caramel/hazelnut dessert spread).

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Svelekake (Norwegian Yogurt Pancakes)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4519163, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Half-boil the potatoes, and drain the water from them.
Transfer the potatoes to a baking dish or pan. Then, place the dish underneath meat roasting on a spit so that they catch the drippings.
Occasionally baste the potatoes with the meat drippings. When they are browned on one side, turn them and brown on the other.
Serve with the roasted meat.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Potatoes Roasted under Meat” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4494732, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Cook the rice.
Cut onion into small cubes and fry in olive oil until brown.
Add water, tomato juice, parsley, soup cube, cheese, garlic, black olives and rice. Season to taste.
Fill into the peppers. Cook for 30 minutes. Rest as above.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Stuffed Peppers (Vegetarian)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4514117, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 2.4 cups (500 g) corn flour for arepas
2.4 cups (500 g) cool water (or more if needed)

instructions.instruction: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, salt, and white cheese. Stir in enough water to make a firm, slightly moist dough.
Cover the dough and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 10 pieces and form each piece into a ball. Flatten the ball slightly.
Preheat the oven to 350 °F (180 °C).
Oil a griddle very lightly and warm it over medium heat. Cook the arepas on the griddle for about 5 minutes on each side, until a golden brown crust forms.
Transfer the arepas to a baking sheet and bake 20–25 minutes, turning them several times as they bake.
Serve immediately, with cheese, ham and black beans.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Cornmeal Pancakes (Arepa)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4628724, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: water for soaking rice, and 2 to 2½ cups for grinding
½ teaspoon yeast or kefir, to start the ferment (optional)

instructions.instruction: Soak the raw rice in water.
Grind the soaked rice until about ¼ ground.
Add the grated coconut along with a little water and continue grinding.
Add the sugar, cooked rice and yeast or kefir, and keep grinding until the whole mixture becomes smooth. It should be thinner than pancake batter.
Transfer it to a wide open container and leave it to rise overnight.
The next morning, add salt and refrigerate the batter until use.
To fry the appams, use a tava or a small bowl-shaped pan with either a non-stick coating or a little oil (coconut or any other refined oil) or ghee.
Pour a full serving spoon of batter into the middle of the pan and swirl it around a single time so that a little of the batter sticks to the sides.
Cover the pan with a hot lid and remove the appam with a spatula after 2–3 minutes, when it becomes slightly browned around the edges. It should be round, with a thick centre and thin, lacy edges.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Appam (Fermented Rice Pancake)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4519100, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 2 lb (1 kg) chicken (cut into small pieces with bone)

instructions.instruction: Cut jackfruit into 1 inch-thick pieces and wash.
Boil jackfruit in water until tender. Drain.
Grind shallots, candle nuts, garlic, salam leaves, and galangal together until fragrant. Add the chicken pieces and toss to coat.
Stir-fry chicken until it changes color. Add 4 cups of water and coconut sugar, and bring to a boil.
Add jackfruit and simmer until chicken and vegetables are tender.
Add coconut milk 5 minutes before it's done; bring back to a boil.
Serve hot with rice.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Gudeg (Green Jackfruit Stew)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4541107, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 2 tablespoons niter kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced clarified butter) or regular butter
1 jalapeño pepper, seeded and finely chopped (optional for spice)
1 teaspoon berbere spice blend, or to taste
4-6 pieces of leftover injera, torn into bite-sized pieces
Fresh cilantro or parsley, chopped, for garnish

instructions.instruction: Heat the niter kibbeh or regular butter in a large skillet or frying pan over medium heat.
Add the finely chopped onion to the pan and sauté until translucent and slightly browned.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and jalapeño pepper (if using) and cook for a few minutes until the tomatoes start to soften.
Sprinkle the berbere spice blend over the mixture and mix well to coat the onions and tomatoes. Adjust the amount of berbere according to your preferred level of spiciness.
Add the torn pieces of injera to the pan and gently toss them with the onion and tomato mixture.
Sauté the mixture for a few minutes, stirring occasionally, until the injera is heated through and slightly crispy.
Season with salt to taste. Keep in mind that injera can be slightly sour, so adjust the salt accordingly.
Remove from heat and transfer to a serving dish. Garnish with freshly chopped cilantro or parsley.
Serve warm as a delicious and satisfying breakfast or brunch option.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Fit-fit (Ethiopian Bread Salad)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4518136, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: Molokhia (Egyptian Jute Mallow Soup)

ingredients.sourceText: 2 cups fresh or frozen jute mallow (molokhia) leaves
Cooked rice or bread for serving

instructions.instruction: If using fresh molokhia leaves, remove any tough stems and wash the leaves thoroughly. If using frozen molokhia, thaw it according to the package instructions.
In a saucepan, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and minced garlic. Sauté until the onion becomes translucent and the garlic becomes fragrant.
Add the fresh or thawed molokhia leaves to the saucepan and stir well to combine with the onion and garlic mixture.
Pour in the vegetable or chicken broth, ensuring that the molokhia leaves are fully submerged.
Season the soup with ground cumin, salt, and black pepper to taste. Stir to incorporate the spices.
Bring the soup to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to low and let it simmer for about 20–30 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld together.
Remove the soup from the heat. Optionally, squeeze the juice of a lemon into the soup and stir well to enhance the flavors.
Serve the molokhia hot, accompanied by cooked rice or bread.

sourceCategories: Recipes using chicken broth and stock

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Molokhia (Egyptian Jute Mallow Soup)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4518457, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 pound (450 g) leg of lamb (shank end), cut into 1½ inch cubes

instructions.instruction: Combine all ingredients except lamb in a gallon size zip-top bag. Add lamb cubes and toss to coat; refrigerate overnight to marinate.
The next day, drain lamb and discard marinade.
Thread 4 lamb cubes onto one skewer. Repeat until all lamb has been skewered.
Fire up a charcoal grill for 15 minutes. Add lamb and cook 8 minutes per side for medium rare.
Serve warm with couscous.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Middle Eastern Lamb Kabobs” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4507348, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Combine the suit, french roll, nutmeg, and lemon zest.
Mix in half a pound of apples, currants, raisins, stoned and chopped, wine, eggs, and a pinch of salt.
Mix all thoroughly together, and boil it in a basin or mould for 3 hours.
Sift fine sugar over it when sent to table, and pour a white wine sauce into the dish.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Windsor Pudding” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4517955, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Peel the apples and bananas. Dice them into small pieces.
Peel and separate the orange sections. Cut sections into smaller pieces if desired.
Cut the cherries into halves or quarters, depending on the size. Pour a bit of the cherry juice in bowl.
Mix everything together, and add orange juice as desired.
If desired, refrigerate prior to serving.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Fruit Salad with Orange Juice” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4518139, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: Table Point Boiled Beef and Vegetables (Tafelspitz)

ingredients.sourceText: 2½ pounds (1200 g) fresh beef brisket, silverside, or sirloin
3 whole cloves garlic, slightly crushed and peeled
3 whole green (freeze dried) or white peppercorns
2 juniper berries (you may substitute with 1 bay leaf)
3 ea. (4 oz / 110 g) whole medium size carrots, peeled and trimmed
1 ea. (2 oz / 55 g) small-medium onion, unpeeled, trimmed, and halved

instructions.instruction: Fill a 5-quart (700 ml) Dutch oven with water, season it with salt, and bring to a rolling boil over medium heat.
When the water boils, add meat, garlic, peppercorns, and juniper berries, then cover the pot.
Bring the water to a boil again and add carrots, onion, and parsley. Cover and let everything simmer for 60 minutes.
Turn the meat over, add salt, and let everything cook, covered, for 90 additional minutes.
Switch off the heat, and let the meat steep for 20 minutes.
Remove the meat from the broth and cut meat across the grain when you serve it.
Serve tafelspitz with apfelkren (see notes) and your choice of raw and cooked vegetables.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Table Point Boiled Beef and Vegetables (Tafelspitz)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4494414, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 2 cups of Silk Nog (vegan eggnog substitute)
1 pint of Soy Dream vanilla ice cream

instructions.instruction: Blend nog and ice cream together in blender.
Pour into a glass, and sprinkle with nutmeg.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Eggnog Milkshake (Vegan)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4480523, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 kolbász (Hungarian sausage) or 1 cup diced ham (optional)
350 grams sour cream around 40% fat (called tejföl or smetana)

instructions.instruction: Cook the potatoes for about 15–20 minutes.
Peel the potatoes and the eggs.
Slice the potatoes, eggs, and sausage.
Put a little olive oil in a baking dish. Arrange alternating layers of potatoes, eggs, and salt or sausage in the dish.
Drizzle olive oil over the filling, and top with sour cream.
Bake in a preheated oven at 200°C for about 35 minutes.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Potato Casserole (Rakott Krumpli)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4592334, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 6 pounds sea bass or cod, cut into slices

instructions.instruction: Fry the onion with the fatty pork. Transfer to a large pot.
Add all remaining ingredients to pot.
Add enough water to cover everything by 1 inch.
Bring to a boil. Simmer for 1 hour, stirring gently every so often.
Serve.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Daniel Webster's Chowder” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4519257, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Combine ingredients in a blender. Add sweetener and variations (below) to taste.
Blend until smooth, roughly 1–2 minutes
Refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight if possible, and use within 5 days.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Rice Milk” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4512994, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: ½ cup evaporated milk or whole milk

instructions.instruction: Combine the flour, baking powder, nutmeg, salt, and sugar in a bowl. Mix in the butter until crumbly. Mix in the egg and evaporated milk to make a dough.
Cover the dough with plastic wrap, and leave to rest for about 5–10 minutes.
While the dough is resting, preheat several inches of vegetable oil in a pot to 350–375°F (medium heat).
Divide the dough into six parts, flouring your palms to prevent the dough from sticking.

Flatten each piece of dough with your hands. Place one boiled egg on the dough, and wrap the dough around the egg to completely enclose it. Pinch the dough to tightly seal it around the egg. Repeat this process until all the eggs are wrapped.
Carefully transfer the egg rolls to the preheated oil, and fry until golden brown.
Remove the egg rolls from the oil, and place on paper towels to remove excess oil.
Serve with the drink of your choice.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Nigerian Egg Roll” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4512727, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 4 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into fries
2 tbsp vegetable oil (plus extra for frying)

instructions.instruction: Peel the potatoes and cut them into thin fries.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan or pot.
Fry the potatoes until golden brown and crispy.
Remove the fries and drain on paper towels.
In a bowl, beat the eggs until well combined.
Add salt and black pepper.
Stir in the onion, tomato, and chili if using.
Add the fried chips to the beaten eggs and mix gently.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Pour the egg and chips mixture into the pan.
Cook for 3–5 minutes until the bottom is golden brown.
Carefully flip the omelette using a plate or lid.
Cook the other side for another 3–4 minutes.
Remove from the heat when fully cooked.
Garnish with fresh coriander.
Cut into wedges and serve hot.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Chipsi mayai” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4638743, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: ½ cup milk (minus ½ tablespoon for the vinegar)

instructions.instruction: Grease or parchment-line some cookie sheets.
Combine the vinegar and milk.
Combine the baking soda, cinnamon, ginger, and 2½ cups of flour.
Cream together the sugar and shortening until well-combined, then beat in the molasses and egg until smooth.
Alternately mix in the dry and milk mixtures, starting and ending with the dry mixture.

Bit by bit, mix in more flour as needed. For drop cookies, you might not add any more. For rolled cookies produced without refrigeration, you are likely to need an extra 1½ cup for a total of 4 cups. Refrigeration can reduce this slightly.
Chill the batter in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.
Form the cookies.
*If making drop cookies, scoop some batter onto the prepared cookie sheet. Using a bit of sugar to prevent sticking, squish the cookie with a glass. Press some toppings into the top of the cookie.

*Plop a pint-sized blob of batter onto a flour-dusted surface. Dust the top of the dough with flour as you squish it down, then roll it out. A cold marble rolling pin is suggested. Cut out shapes, then place them on the cookie sheet. The unused dough may be put back into the mix; note that this increases the proportion of flour.
Bake cookies for 8–10 minutes at 375°F.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Molasses Cookies” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4517104, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: Tomato Basil Soup with Garlic Toasts

ingredients.sourceText: 4 ea. ½-inch thick slices either French or Italian crusty white bread, cut on the bias

instructions.instruction: Combine paste, juice, cream, broth, 2 tsp salt, 2 tsp pepper, and diced tomatoes in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium high heat.
Reduce heat to medium low and cook, stirring occasionally, until liquid has reduced by ⅓.
Using an immersion blender, purée soup until smooth. Keep warm over low heat.
Toast bread slices in the toaster oven. The second they come out, brush slices with olive oil and sprinkle with garlic and remaining salt and pepper. Set aside.
Add basil leaves to tomato purée and let steep for 5 minutes over low heat. Remove leaves.
Garnish individual bowls with sprigs of basil and serve warm with garlic toast.

sourceCategories: Recipes using chicken broth and stock

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Tomato Basil Soup with Garlic Toasts” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4512031, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 3 Honeycrisp apples, peeled, cored, and sliced into 12ths

instructions.instruction: Melt 1 tbsp butter in a stainless steel skillet over medium heat. Add apples and sauté just until browned around edges. Remove and keep warm.
Meanwhile, combine liqueurs. Add to pan, turn heat off, and ignite. Bring to a boil and start scraping browned bits.
Add remaining ingredients to pan and bring to a boil over medium heat until reduced by ⅓.
Add apples and toss to coat.
Serve warm.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Coffee Rum Glazed Apples” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4515825, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 2 slabs St. Louis style/cut pork spareribs

instructions.instruction: Season ribs with the barbecue rub. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Place chunks into the firebox of a 250°F smoker or the coal area of a 250°F charcoal grill set for indirect heat.
Place ribs into food box or on top of the grate of the charcoal grill, cover, and cook, basting often with sauce, for 5–6 hours.
Brush sauce generously on top and bottom of ribs then place on a medium high grill, continually brushing with sauce until well browned, then flip and repeat 1 more time.
Place remaining sauce into a squirt bottle. Meanwhile, remove ribs and let rest for 10 minutes.
Serve with sauce in a squirt bottle.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Southern Barbecue Ribs” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4497761, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: ½ cup karkashi leaves, either fresh or dried and ground

instructions.instruction: Grind the karkashi leaves to a paste.
Bring the water to boil in a pot, and stir in the fermented locust beans.
Add the fish and meat, and cook for 5–7 minutes.
Add the karkashi leaf paste along with the potash. Stir, and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the seasoning cube. Continue stirring with a whisk for 3 minutes until the mixture is smooth.
Serve the soup with tuwo masara, tuwo dawa, tuwo alkama, or tuwo shinkafa.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Miyan Karkashi (Nigerian Sesame Leaf Soup)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4636092, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 100 ml (½ cup) uncooked Japanese-style short grain rice
Filling of choice, such as any of the following:
Canned tuna, mixed with mayonnaise and seasoned to taste with chopped leeks, soy sauce, or chilies; sour or salty flavours work well.
Katsuobushi, moistened with a small amount of soy sauce

instructions.instruction: Cook the rice according to package or rice cooker directions. Let cool just enough to handle with your hands.
While the rice is cooking, prepare your fillings.
Fill a bowl with salt water to rinse your fingers and season the onigiri. You can fill and shape the onigiri using two different methods:

* Method 1: Wet your hands in the salt water. Take two large spoonfuls of rice into one hand (carefully; the rice is hot), and gently squeeze and flatten it with the other. Make an indentation in the middle, and put some of the filling into the center. Be a little careful to get the filling only in the center and not all over the ball; that can make the rice less sticky, and stickiness is good. "Fold" the rice over the filling so it becomes covered. Squeeze gently, and mold it into a triangular shape by folding both your hands along the palms while keeping the fingers straight. Squeeze like that, rotating the ball a few times, and you will soon have a very neat triangle—this really is much harder to explain than to do. Once the ball is done, put it down on a clean surface to cool down. Rinse your hands in the salt water and repeat.

* Method 2: Use a bowl and some plastic film. Place about ⅔ of the mixture into the centre of the cling wrap that has been draped into the bowl loosely. Then, add approximately 2 teaspoons of filling (this is working off of about 3–4 portions per cup of rice. Then, place the last ⅓ of the rice to the top. Then, mould the onigiri within the cling wrap. This drastically reduces mess and also is slightly more 'kid friendly'.

Once the balls are reasonably cool, you need to protect them from drying out. The easiest way is to wrap them in cling wrap, or put them into an airtight plastic food container. When it is time to eat, take one rice ball, wrap it in a piece of nori, and eat away. If you don't mind soggy nori, you can wrap the balls in nori beforehand.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Onigiri” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4508978, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Place bacon in a sheet pan.
Set the broiler to 'low'.
Pre-cook the bacon under the broiler until it is about halfway done.
While bacon cooks, place white bread on a sheet, one slice per diner.
Place a slice of American cheese on each slice of bread.
Place the tomato slices on each sandwich
Sprinkle a small amount of onion onto each sandwich.
Place a strip of half-cooked bacon on each sandwich.
Place the cookie sheet under broiler, set to maximum temperature, and broil for approximately 3–4 minutes. You must check on them often to prevent burning.
Remove once the bread is toasted, the cheese is golden at the edges, and the bacon is fully cooked.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Red Devils” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4518276, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 whole chicken, cut up (or any 8 chicken pieces—any combination of leg, breast, thigh, and wing)

instructions.instruction: In a blender or food processor, combine parsley, shallots, garlic, olive oil, mustard, Italian herb blend, lemon juice, pepper, and salt. Purée.
Transfer mixture to a gallon zip-lock bag.
Add chicken, making sure it's covered on all sides by the marinade.
Seal bag and refrigerate for an hour.
Preheat oven to 300°F (150C).
Transfer chicken pieces to a rimmed baking sheet.
Bake about 40 minutes, turning pieces after 20 minutes, until juices run clear.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Mediterranean Green Chicken” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4613415, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 75 g sieved icing sugar or caster sugar

instructions.instruction: Cream together the butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Gradually beat in the brandy.
Chill before serving.
Serve with Christmas pudding and warm mince pies.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Brandy Butter” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4523688, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 500 ml Iraqi dates, chopped and seeded

instructions.instruction: Boil dates in lightly salted water stirring frequently until it is a thick paste.
Mix in finely chopped nuts.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Charoset (Iraqi)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4630111, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Slice the tomatoes ¼–½ inch (0.75–1.25 cm) thick.
Salt and pepper tomato slices to taste.
Dip slices in cornmeal and shallow fry in hot grease or oil over medium heat for about 3 minutes or until golden on bottom.
Gently turn over, and fry the other side.
Serve by themselves or, for a elegant addition, add a little goat cheese.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Fried Green Tomatoes” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4493816, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Cook the pasta as directed on the packaging. Drain.
Combine the eggs, milk, salt, and pepper in a mixing bowl.
Mix in the grated cheese.
Melt the butter and add to the mixture.
Boil a small amount of water and add the stock, then stir it into the mixture.
Stir in the grated zucchini, then the drained pasta.
Grease a baking or casserole dish, and spread the ingredients from the bowl evenly in it.
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for about 30 minutes, or until the pasta bake is firm all the way through.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Zucchini Pasta Bake” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4525784, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 675 g (1.5 lb) skinless and boneless chicken breast, diced into cubes
4 large cloves of garlic, finely chopped
1–4 chopped fresh red chillis (depending on strength of the chillis and the desired strength of the marinade)
1 tsp salt (use rock salt for best results)

instructions.instruction: Add all of the ingredients except the chicken to a non-metallic mixing bowl, and mix well.
Add the chicken and mix until fully coated.

Ideally, the chicken should now be left in a refrigerator to marinate for at least 24 hours. It may not be safe to leave chicken which has previously been frozen for longer than 24 hours, but fresh chicken should be left to marinate for 48 hours for best results. If you do not wish to leave the chicken to marinate, simply continue to the next step.

For best results, place on skewers and cook in a tandoor or ceramic pot oven. The chicken can also be cooked on skewers under a medium grill for 5–8 minutes on each side or barbecued (cooking times depend on the temperature of the barbecue). Always ensure the chicken is cooked throughout before serving. It should come apart easily when pressed down with the side of a fork.
Serve with naan, with rice or use in a Chicken Tikka Masala.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Chicken Tikka” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4615207, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 ea. (4 pounds) boneless pork loin roast
¼ cup crushed ginger snap cookies

instructions.instruction: Combine salt, honey, vinegar, and wine in a gallon size zip-top bag. Add ice and shake until ice is mostly melted and mixture has cooled down.
Add pork loin and refrigerate 2 ½–3 hours.
Drain pork and pat dry. Discard remaining brine. Set aside.
Combine remaining ingredients except mustard. Brush pork with mustard and press spice mixture into all sides of meat.
Place roast on a roasting rack in a roasting pan. Insert a probe thermometer into the center and bake at 410°F until internal temperature reaches 140°F for medium rare.
Remove to a plate and let rest 10 minutes before carving. Serve warm.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Holiday Pork Loin” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4615194, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 800 g (1.75 lb) fresh salmon filet, approximately 2–5 cm (1–2 inches) thick
5 ml (1 tsp) whole or crushed white pepper

instructions.instruction: Cut the salmon filet into two equally-sized parts (if you are making gravlax for many people it is fine to use two filets instead). Freeze the salmon for at least 4 days at -18°C or colder to kill any parasites.
After deep freezing the salmon remove it from the freezer and let it thaw, preferably overnight in the refrigerator. The salmon does not have to be completely thawed for the next steps.
Combine the salt and sugar. Place the salmon, skin down, on a table. Rub the salt and sugar mix onto the pieces, then apply the juniper berries and pepper. Finally, cover with dill.
Put one salmon piece on top of another, flesh side to flesh side so the skin it outside on both pieces, and place in a plastic bag. Add any leftover ingredients to the bag along with the gin.
Seal the bag and place it in the refrigerator. Let the salmon cure in the mixture, turning the bag over once, preferably twice, a day for 4 days.

After 4 days, the salmon is ready to serve. If you are not going to eat it immediately (it lasts a couple of days) move it to a fresh plastic bag or jar, removing the salty liquid that has formed in the original bag. If you keep it in the original bag the risk is that it may be too salty once you are about to serve it.

Use a sharp knife to slice thin slices from the salmon at an angle. During slicing, also remove any remaining bones. The larger the piece of salmon the larger the angle and the larger surface area for the produced slices. Large slices look better when served.

As a main dish, serve with potato stew, boiled potatoes and gravlax sauce, or in a salad. As an appetizer, serve on crispbread or toast. Potato stew with some additional Dijon mustard is excellent addition to gravlax.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Gravlax” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4508844, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 pound meat (beef, chicken, or goat), cut into pieces, or fish (tilapia or catfish), cleaned and gutted

instructions.instruction: In a large pot, heat the palm oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onions and minced garlic to the pot. Sauté until the onions are soft and translucent.
If using meat, add the meat pieces to the pot and cook until they are browned on all sides.
Pour in the chicken broth or water and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Add the diced tomato, bell pepper, and chopped hot pepper (if using) to the pot. Stir well to combine with the other ingredients.
Gently add the diced eggplant to the pot and stir to incorporate with the other ingredients.
Season the stew with ground pepper and salt to taste. Adjust the seasoning according to your preference.
Let the stew simmer for about 20–25 minutes or until the eggplant is tender and cooked through.
Stir occasionally during cooking to prevent sticking and to ensure even cooking.
Remove the pot from the heat and let the stew rest for a few minutes before serving.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Liberian Eggplant Stew” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4629625, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 cup (60 g / 2.1 oz) puffed rice cereal
½ cup (50 g / 1.8 oz) chopped nuts
1 small bag (50 g / 1.8 oz) semi-sweet chocolate chips

instructions.instruction: Melt the semi-sweet chocolate chips in a double boiler.
Put all other ingredients into a bowl. Mix.
Form the mixture into small balls, about half the size of a golf ball.
If desired, refrigerate or freeze the peanut butter balls for easier dipping.
Dip the balls in the melted chocolate and place on wax paper.
Allow the chocolate balls to cool in the freezer or fridge before consumption.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Chocolate Balls” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4517465, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: After properly cleaning the rice, add it to a saucepan of water. When the rice is tender, add salt and bring to a boil. Give it a good five to seven minutes.
To make the rice smooth, mash it with a wooden spoon or a small pestle.
Pour cold water into a cup and place it near the pan. Transfer the rice to a serving dish after scooping it with wet hands and rolling it into balls.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Omo tuo” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4612965, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 pound (½ kilogram) dry yellow split peas

instructions.instruction: Soak split peas up to six hours in cold water if you wish. This is not necessary, but will shorten cooking time.
Put all ingredients into a 6 or 8 quart stock pot or Dutch oven
Bring to a boil, then simmer covered until peas are tender, 1–2 hours.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Yellow Split Pea Soup” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4525778, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Mix together flour, baking powder, and sugar.
Mix soy milk into the dry mixture.
Heat a griddle until water sprinkled on it quickly evaporates. Spread a thin film of oil on the griddle.
Pour pancake batter on griddle to form 2–3-inch circles. Bubbles should start forming.
When the underside is light brown, flip the pancake.
When the other side is light brown, serve.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Whole Wheat Pancakes (Vegan)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4525775, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Mix water, oat flakes, and salt in a bowl.
Boil on high heat for 2–3 minutes.
Stir and serve immediately.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Microwave Oat Porridge” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4517857, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Heat some oil in a pan over high heat. Add the tomatoes, and fry until well-heated.
Beat the eggs, and stir in the cooked tomato. Return the mixture to the pan over medium-low heat, making sure it is evenly spread across the pan. Cook until the egg is sturdy enough to flip.
Flip the omelette to the other side, and cook until the bottom is golden.
Serve hot with bread or jollof rice.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Nigerian Tomato Omelette” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4493957, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 2 cups (480 ml) fresh parsley, finely chopped
1 large tomato, diced with seeds discarded
⅓ cup (80 ml) extra virgin olive oil
½ cup (120 ml) fresh lemon juice

instructions.instruction: Boil 2–3 cups of water
Once water comes to a boil, add bulgur wheat and remove from heat. Let cool.
Drain the bulgur wheat, and mix wheat with all other ingredients.
Refrigerate.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Tabbouleh VI” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4518082, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 can cream of mushroom soup or cream of chicken soup

instructions.instruction: Brown hamburger and drain.
Mix in cream of mushroom or cream of chicken soup.
Put mixture in casserole dish and cover the top with one layer of tater tots.
Bake at 350 F for 1 hour or until done.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Tater Tot Casserole” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4523451, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Combine the oil, vinegar, rosemary, and pepper. Add salmon steaks, and marinate for 15 minutes.
Place the steaks on a hot grill, cooking on each side for 3 minutes until flaky.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Rosemary Grilled Salmon Steaks” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4508858, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 4 oz (110 g) bittersweet chocolate, chopped (can substitute semisweet)

instructions.instruction: Place the milk and cinnamon in a saucepan, and gently heat to just below a simmer, about 180 F.
Add the chocolate, and stir while allowing to melt. Do not allow to come to a boil.
When the chocolate has melted, strain the chocolate milk into another container, add the extracts, and whisk or blend until frothy.
Transfer to mugs or heatproof glasses and serve.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Hot Chocolate (Orange)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4524022, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 ham bone or a rough equivalent of salt bacon
A very small amount (3 oz / ~90 g) of that day's brewed coffee (optional)

instructions.instruction: Wash beans carefully and soak overnight in 8 cups of water.
Drain and refill with 5 cups of water.
Add all the other ingredients.
Bring to a boil and simmer at least 1 hour, or until tender.
Remove bay leaves.
Do not drain prior to serving, the liquid is an important aspect of the dish.
Can be served using slotted spoon, to allow draining, or with a ladle into small side-dish bowls

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Central Texan Pinto Beans” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4629680, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: ½ teaspoon garam masala or good curry powder

instructions.instruction: Cut banana in 2 cm slices.
Add milk, cream, garam masala (or curry) powder, chili, and lemon (add some salt) to the bananas.
Melt butter, add cumin seeds and turmeric, and cook at medium low for a couple of minutes until a fragrant smell develops.
Add bananas and their sauce.
Cook on a gentle flame until ready (depends on banana's ripeness)—do not overcook.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Banana Curry” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4517517, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Crack the eggs and separate the egg yolk from the egg whites.
Place the egg whites into the bowl, and whip the egg whites with a whisk until soft and fluffy.
Briefly whisk the egg yolks, then gently fold them into the whipped whites.
Pour into a frying pan over low heat, and cook slowly on the stove until the bottom is golden brown.
Place the frying pan into the oven after taking it off the stove, and bake until it is golden brown on the top.
Pull out of the oven and unmold onto a plate.
Pour and spread the jam gently over the omelette. Sift some icing sugar over the top of it.
Enjoy!

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Sweet Omelette” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4540922, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 cup evaporated milk or condensed milk
¼ cup sugar (adjust according to taste)

instructions.instruction: In a blender, combine the baobab fruit pulp and water. Blend on high speed until the mixture is smooth and well-combined.
Place a strainer or cheesecloth over a pitcher or jug, and pour the blended mixture through it. This will help remove any pulp or seeds, resulting in a smoother juice.
Add the evaporated milk or condensed milk to the pitcher, along with the sugar and vitamin C powder (if using). Stir well until the sugar is dissolved and the ingredients are thoroughly mixed.
Refrigerate the bouye juice for at least 1 hour to chill and allow the flavors to meld together.
Once chilled, give the juice a good stir before serving.
Pour the juice into glasses filled with ice cubes.
Garnish each glass with fresh mint leaves for added freshness and aroma.
Serve the bouye juice immediately and enjoy its refreshing and creamy goodness.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Gambian Baobab Juice (Bouye)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4541056, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: Corn on the Cob with Husks

ingredients.sourceText: Corn on the cob, with husks left on

instructions.instruction: Carefully peel back husk without detaching it and remove silk.
Replace husks and soak ears in cold water for ½ hour.
Place corn on grill or on a rack above an open fire.
Cook for about 15 minutes, turning occasionally to ensure even cooking.
Serve with butter and salt.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Corn on the Cob with Husks” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4495034, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 pint (570 ml) milk, part cream if the person is not forbidden that

instructions.instruction: Heat the milk to the simmering point.
Generously butter the toast slices.
Heat a pretty bowl, deeper than it is wide. Break the hot buttered toast into it, pour the steaming but not boiling milk over it, sprinkle a little salt and pepper on the top, and serve at once.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Milk Toast I” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4511231, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 cup (125 g/4.4 oz) uncooked brown rice or white rice

instructions.instruction: Find a large saucepan or frying pan which has a lid, and place over medium heat.
Add butter then chopped onion to pan. Cook the onion for a couple of minutes until it starts to brown slightly.
Add curry powder, and stir for a minute.
Mix in vegetarian bouillon cubes, raisins, rice, and water.
Put on pan lid and simmer until water is absorbed (about 15 minutes).

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Curried Rice” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4513598, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Select medium-sized tomatoes and hollow out the centers, reserving the pulp.
Mix the crumbs, cheese, salt, pepper, butter, and hot water with the pulp from the centers of the tomatoes.
Fill the tomatoes with this stuffing, place in a pan, and bake in a moderate oven until the tomato can be pierced easily with a fork.
Serve hot.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Tomatoes with Cheese Stuffing” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4523450, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Cut the olives in half.
Cut the turkey into ¾-inch chunks.
Mix the olives and tomato paste.
Mix in turkey, adding as much as will be covered by the paste.
Optionally, warm the mixture.
Place some of the mixture on a tortilla.
Wrap the tortilla around the mixture.
Place the finished wrap on an ungreased cookie sheet, with the exposed edge (flap) downward to prevent the wrap from coming undone before it is cooked.
Keep making wraps as needed.
Place the cookie sheet in an oven set to 350°F.
Remove the wraps when they start to brown, which should be about 15 minutes.
Let the wraps cool a bit on the outside while heat sinks into the inside.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Turkey Wrap” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4518297, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: Shrimp and Cheese Grits
timeSourceText: 20 minutesor 40 minutes if you have to peel the shrimp

ingredients.sourceText: ½ large sweet onion, cut into thin strips
½ yellow bell pepper, cut into strips
½ red bell pepper, cut into strips
¼–½ teaspoon hot sauce, or to taste (optional)

instructions.instruction: Fry bacon until crisp, remove and set aside.
Sauté onions, garlic, and peppers in bacon grease, add lime juice and hot sauce and set aside.
Prepare grits per the directions on box. Add cheese and butter when done cooking to allow for them to melt, then set aside.
Stir when done melting.
Sauté the shrimp until they turn pink, about 2–3 minutes.
Place the grits and cheese in large serving container and place the shrimp down the center of the container.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Shrimp and Cheese Grits” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4525178, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: Mineral water (optional, makes the dough more fluffy)

instructions.instruction: Mix the flour with the milk, stirring thoroughly. Mix in the eggs one-by-one, then stir in the salt and rum. If desired, thin the batter with a bit of mineral water.
Heat the pan well. Add a drop of oil and rub it over the pan with a kitchen towel.

Ladle a dipperful of the batter into the pan, tilting the pan so that the batter spreads as evenly as possible over the whole pan. Alternatively, you can accomplish this by using a special wooden tool used to spread crêpes.
Let cook about 45 seconds to 1 minute until the top of the palatschinke is dry.
Flip the pancake over, and allow it to brown for about 30 seconds on the other side. Remove from the pan, and set aside.
Repeat the cooking process until you have used up all the batter.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Palatschinken (Czech/Austrian Crepes)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4535125, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: ¾ cup (150 g) white granulated sugar

instructions.instruction: Add eggs and sugar to a bowl, and whisk rapidly until mixture turns pale.
Whisk in the citrus zests.
Combine the almond meal, cinnamon, and salt in a separate bowl. Transfer to the egg mixture, and use a rubber spatula to gently fold everything together until well combined.
Butter and flour the springform pan, then pour in the batter. Smooth the top if necessary.
Bake in preheated oven at 360ºF (180ºC) for 40 minutes or until golden brown and fully cooked in the center.
Cool completely, and unmold the cake.
Place a Santiago cross cut-out on top of the cake, then dust generous amount of icing sugar all over cake.
Carefully remove the cross cut-out. Slice and serve.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Tarta de Santiago” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4516963, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: Sweet Mole with Vanilla Bean Ice Cream

ingredients.sourceText: 4 ounces semi-sweet dark chocolate bar, cut into pieces
2 cups high-quality vanilla bean ice cream

instructions.instruction: Wash, devein, and remove seeds from chile ancho.
Boil the chile, then blend with the smallest amount of water possible.
Strain off water.
In a saucepan, add pureed chile, piloncillo, clove, cinnamon and chocolate.
Boil for 3 minutes.
Remove clove.
To serve, allow vanilla ice cream to soften slightly in a bowl and stir in mole.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Sweet Mole with Vanilla Bean Ice Cream” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4587356, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 4 hamburger buns, split in half and toasted

instructions.instruction: Form meat into 4 equal patties, about ¾ inch thick. Make a depression in the center with your thumb and set aside.
Brush patties with oil. Sprinkle on both sides with seasonings.

Preheat grill. Add patties and cook, turning often, until desired "doneness" is achieved. Remove to a plate, top each with a slice of cheese, and cover tightly with aluminum foil. Let rest until cheese is melted.
Brush cut sides of bread with oil. Add a patty onto the bottom half of a bun, then top with the upper half. Repeat with remaining meat and serve immediately.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Smokehouse Burgers” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4600880, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Pour water into a saucepan, add anise seeds, and bring to a boil over medium heat.
Turn off the heat, cover, and leave to infuse for 30 minutes.
Filter out the seeds.
Add the sugar as desired, and bring to boil again over medium heat. Simmer until the syrup drips into a thin stream.
Filter a second time.
Let it cool and bottle. Serve with very cold sparkling or still water according to preference.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Habet Hlawa (Algerian Anise Beverage)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4508222, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 loaf of white, pappy sort of bread or brioche, crusts removed and sliced
1 bottle of the best quality blackcurrant cordial you can find, in reserve

instructions.instruction: Liberally butter the inside a pudding bowl about 5 inches in diameter. The bowl should preferably not be greater in diameter that the size of your pieces of sliced bread. If you are worried about getting the whole thing out of the bowl in one piece, line the bowl first with some cling film. It's a fiddly job, but ensures you get a perfect shape at the end.

Combine the blackcurrants, redcurrants, mint leaves, lime zest, sugar, and about 3 tbsp water. Poach them for about 5 minutes on the lowest possible heat setting of your stove. Add the strawberries and poach for another minute.
Turn the heat off and add the raspberries. Leave to cool.
Using the prepared bowl as a guide, cut a circle out of the white bread the same diameter as the top of the bowl. Do the same with the bottom of the bowl.

Using a sharp knife, slice the bread into squares or oblongs, roughly the same height as the bowl, which will be used to line the inside of the bowl. This does not have to be an exact science. In simple terms what we are trying to do is to line the bowl with the white bread.

Lay the smaller circle of white bread on the bottom of the bowl. Put the oblongs of white bread up the side of the bowl, overlapping slightly, and pour the fruit mixture into the void right up to the top. The bread should become well soaked in the juice from the cooked fruit. Indeed if there is not enough juice to soak the bread so it turns very red, use the cordial as a top-up.
Place the large circle, or disc, of bread on the top and press it down well.
Top with a weight or something that fits into the top of the bowl so it squashes everything down tight, and place it in the fridge for at least 40 minutes.

When you are ready to serve the pudding, carefully using a knife to release the bread mould from the side of the bowl, and invert the whole thing onto a plate. If things become a little fraught and wobbly at this point, don't panic—just sort of whack everything back into shape using a wooden spoon.
Decorate your plate with some more summer fruit, maybe a couple of mint leaves, and an artistic dollop of fresh whipped cream or crème fraîche, then serve with a flourish.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Summer Pudding” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4587366, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Wash the rice with several changes of cold water. Drain.
Add the water, bay leaf, peppercorns, cinnamon, cloves and salt and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium low and cook covered for about 12 minutes until all the water has evaporated and the rice grains are tender yet separate.
Heat the oil in a pan.
Add the tofu and shallow-fry until for a few minutes on each side.
Scoop out of the oil and set aside.
To the same oil, add the nuts and the raisins and shallow-fry until the nuts are golden brown and the raisins have plumped up.
Remove from heat.
Turn the rice into a serving bowl and fluff gently with a fork.
Fold in the tofu and the nuts gently and mix well.
Serve hot.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Rice with Tofu and Nuts” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4513695, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 hot banana pepper, seeded and chopped

instructions.instruction: Blanch, peel, and pit peaches.
Coarsely chop peaches and combine with lemon juice in a large stainless steel or enamel saucepan. Stir in sugar.
Bring to a boil and cook, stirring frequently until the peaches are tender (about 15 minutes).
Add remaining ingredients. Boil over medium-high heat for about 45 minutes or until thick, stirring frequently.
Ladle chutney into six hot, sterilized, 1-pint (2-cup) preserving jars, leaving ½ inch of headspace. Wipe rims clean and seal according to manufacturer's directions.
Process for 15 minutes in a boiling water bath. Allow chutney to mature for at least one month before using.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Peach Chutney” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4615132, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 2 tablespoons pork fat or some type of oil (optional)
1.5–2 lbs (700–900 g) smoked pork neck bone (optional, or, may substitute a much smaller amount of sausage)
¼ teaspoon cayenne pepper (powder or flakes; optional)
1 medium onion (optional), diced, chopped, or sliced

instructions.instruction: Thoroughly wash the collard greens with very slightly soapy water, and rinse clean with plain water. Rinse at least twice to ensure removal of all grit and soap.
Leaves may be stripped from stems or left on if preferred. If left on, cut stems in small length (under 1 inch / 2.5 cm) for ease.
Chop leaves into bite-sized pieces. They may be folded lengthwise or widthwise to facilitate this.

Place chopped leaves into pot of boiling water—use just enough water to keep the greens off of the bottom of the pot; or else your greens will be watery and will have no flavor. Leaves will reduce in size while cooking, though not significantly. Depending on the size of the pot in which they're cooked, it may be necessary to cook some, then add more leaves after a brief time.
Add remaining ingredients.
Boil for approximately 20 minutes or until they reach desired tenderness. If overcooked, their taste will not be affected, but they'll be mushy.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Boiled Collard Greens” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4504835, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Purée all ingredients together in a blender.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Creamy Delight Smoothie” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4524019, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 2 ounces (60 ml) liquid yeast or 2 Tbsp (15 ml) dry yeast granules
½–¾ cup (120–180 ml) white sugar for colouring

instructions.instruction: Clean and wash grapes well, removing stalks and any debris.
Crush the grapes until you get a good purple colour.
Place the crushed grapes in a ceramic jar, and mix with 2 kg sugar. Mix in the water, egg whites, yeast, and wheat until well-combined.
Cover with an airtight lid, and let ferment in a cool place for 21 days, stirring well every other day.
Strain the mixture and discard the solids.
Stir the remaining sugar into the liquid, and place back in the fermenting container. Mix well, and keep airtight for another 21 days to ferment.
Filter the wine using a muslin cloth.
Place the sugar for colouring in a heavy bottomed pot over medium heat. Stir until the sugar melts and becomes a dark brown caramel—do not let it burn.
Remove the caramel from the heat, and gradually and carefully stir in 5–7 Tbsp hot water. Let cool slightly.
Stir the caramel syrup into the wine, then transfer the wine into a jar for storage.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Homemade Red Wine” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4514566, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 2 cups (450 g / 16 oz) white granulated sugar
1 cup (325 g / 11.5 oz) liquid honey (any variety)

instructions.instruction: In a 3–4-quart (2.8–3.8 L) heavy-bottomed saucepan, combine the sugar, salt, and cornstarch until uniform.
Using a wooden or metal spoon, stir in the honey and the water. Place the saucepan over medium-high heat and continually stir until all the sugar dissolves.
Continue to stir the mixture until the mixture begins to boil. Once boiling begins, let the solution cook undisturbed until it reaches 270°F/132°C also known as the soft crack stage. Add the butter.
Remove the hot mixture from heat and pour onto a greased, lipped cookie sheet, a greased marble slab, or a silicone mat, such as a Silpat.

When taffy is cool enough to handle with greased cleaned hands, gather the taffy and continually stretch, fold and recombine it until it lightens in color and gains a satiny gloss. This step is best accomplished with a friend and requires 10–15 minutes of continuous pulling.

Once taffy has been properly pulled, roll into ½-inch ropes and cut into 1 in long pieces with a knife or greased scissors. Once all the taffy is cut, wrap in small squares of waxed paper and twist the ends.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Honey Taffy” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4523491, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: ½ cup (120 ml) vegetable oil (for frying)
360 grams (about ¾ lb) ground fish or fish paste (pla kuud)

instructions.instruction: Stack the lime leaves and roll them together into a tube shape. Slice them into thin strips.
Slice the green beans into small (½ inch) pieces.
Mince the fish.
Mix all the ingredients except the green beans and lime leaves in a bowl.
Stir until the mixture is smooth.
Add the green beans and lime leaves to the mixture and stir again.
Add the oil to a frying pan and heat to a medium temperature.
Drop a tablespoon of the mixture into the pan and flatten slightly. When the bottom is cooked, turn over.
When cooked on both sides, place on a paper towel to drain any extra oil. Continue with the rest of the mixture.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Tod Mun (Thai Fish Cakes)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4535142, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Combine salt, peppers, and ½ cup flour. Coat okra with flour mixture.
Dip okra into hot sauce and dredge in remaining flour, adding more as needed. Let rest 2–3 minutes.
Heat oil in a large pot or a deep-fryer to 375°F. Add okra, 6 at a time, and fry 3–4 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Drain on a cooling rack and repeat until all okra has been fried.
Sprinkle fried okra with additional kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper and serve warm.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Spicy Fried Okra” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4503245, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Remove extra stem endings, yellow leaves, and damaged parts from all herbs and wash them thoroughly. Drain.
Remove roots from green onions and radishes and majority of radish leaves (leaving only the younger ones). Wash them thoroughly and drain.
Mix them up or arrange them on a plate.
Eat raw and enjoy!

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Kanachi (Armenian Herb Salad)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4518146, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 200 g (7.1 oz / 2 ea.) apples, roughly chopped
170 g (6 oz / ¾ cup) white granulated sugar

instructions.instruction: Add your ingredients into a bowl, mixing until combined but not overworking your mixture.
Butter your mould of choice, and sprinkle a little flour inside.
Place your mixture into your mould, and place a piece of baking paper on top.
Cover with a cloth, and tie to secure.
Boil or steam your mixture for 3 hours.
Serve hot with custard or a wine sauce.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Eve's Pudding (Hartshorne)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4587463, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 package (12 ounces) dark or bittersweet chocolate chips, divided in half

instructions.instruction: Let the eggs and butter sit out for 30 minutes to bring to room temperature.
Preheat oven to 165°C (325°F).
In a small bowl, sift together the flour, baking soda, and salt. Set aside.
In a small saucepan combine butter, sugar, and water. Bring just to a boil then remove from heat.
Add half of the chocolate chips (6 oz) and vanilla. Stir until smooth and shiny.
Transfer the chocolate mixture into a large bowl.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Gradually blend in flour mixture.
Stir in remaining chocolate chips and nuts if desired.
Spread in a greased 9-inch square pan.
Bake at 165°C (325°F) for 30–35 minutes.
Cool completely before cutting into 2¼-inch squares.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Double Chocolate Brownies” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4587112, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Cream the butter and sugar together.
Beat in the eggs.
Combine the flour, cream of tartar, and baking soda.
Alternately mix the flour and milk into the batter to make a dough.
Drop dough on a greased or lined baking sheet in spoonfuls.
Sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon.
Bake in a quick oven.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Snickerdoodles (Boston Globe)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4523380, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Chop cucumbers and radishes into small cubes (about ¼ inch on the side).
Chop green onions.
Combine all of the above in an appropriately sized bowl.
Add sour cream and mix well.
Add salt to taste and mix again.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Cucumber and Radish Salad” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4518123, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Mash the smoked fish in a bowl.
Add the garri, ground kuli kuli, sliced onions, salt, and dry pepper.
Stir the ingredients together and serve.

provenance.attributionText: Adapted from “Kwado (Nigerian Cassava Flour Salad)” by Wikibooks contributors, revision 4494248, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

instructions.instruction: Heat a large non-stick skillet or griddle over low heat while preparing ingredients.
Mix flour, salt, baking powder, and baking soda in medium bowl.
